statute: Gov. Code 12580 et seq.; 12599 (commercial fundraiser), 12599.1 (fundraising counsel), 12599.2 (coventurer), 12599.9-12599.10 (platforms, AB 488); 11 CCR 314-323
professional_solicitor_or_fundraiser: Commercial fundraiser: register; 10 working days' notice before solicitation
solicitor_fundraiser_bond_usd: 25000 (survey lists the bond against commercial fundraisers and fundraising counsel together; the split by role is not verified at statute level)
commercial_coventurer: Register unless written contract + all funds transferred within 90 days + written accounting (12599.2)
online_platform_law: Yes: charitable fundraising platforms (CFP) and platform charities must register (PL-1, $625 fee per secondary source); Types A-E incl. 'recommended donations' and Type E white-label SaaS licensed to charities
platform_law_status: In force: registration 2024-06-12; consent, receipts and remittance timing 2025-01-01
daf_sponsor_exclusion_in_platform_law: Conditional: sponsor excluded only if it does not list or name charities for solicitation to persons without advisory privileges in its DAFs
tech_vendor_exclusion_in_platform_law: Yes, for a vendor that 'solely provides technical or supportive services' (hosting, payment processing). The vendor becomes a CFP for its own platform if it solicits there
enforcement_2021plus_against_giving_plat: Flipcause C&D 2025-11-12 (not registered as a platform; unremitted funds). 37 of 205 vetted platforms (18%) unregistered as of Nov 2025 per press; the AG reportedly did not penalize registrations made before 2024-10-12
non_custodial_daf_vendor_exposure_infere: HIGH relevance. A non-custodial vendor that runs a donor-facing grant-recommendation or charity-search app, or licenses a white-label giving app to a sponsor, may itself be a CFP (Type A or E). The DAF exclusion protects the sponsor, not its vendor. Payment-processor-style back-end only = excluded [inference]
evidence_label: confirmed (statute/regs via FindLaw + OAG regs PDF); secondary (survey bond detail)

online_platform_law: Yes: CFPs must register with the AG ($250 per secondary source), renew by July 1, file annual reports. Online charitable sales promotions for 7+ charities a year are regulated as CFPs
platform_law_status: In force 2026-07-01 (effective date extended in June 2025)
non_custodial_daf_vendor_exposure_infere: MEDIUM-HIGH. Hawaii's FAQ says a platform 'may be a CFP even if it does not itself ask for the donation' [quoted via FKKS]. Exclusions for DAF sponsors or vendors were not verified [unknown]
evidence_label: secondary (law-firm summary of AG FAQ); survey
